verdicts.reason: A reads left to right as a banner should (logo, headline, CTA), but the SOLSTICE logo is shrunk to a tiny, barely legible mark, the CTA is broken onto two lines, and a bokeh dot sits on 'Line'. B stacks a tiny logo over a headline that sits left of the canvas centre, then jams a two-line CTA against the right edge with a dot on 'Line', so the layout looks lopsided and unplanned.

A puts the headline on the left and stacks the logo over a single-line CTA on the right, which gives clean grouping and keeps the CTA readable, though the logo floating above the CTA is a weak pairing and the left side has a lot of empty space. B has the same flaws as pair 1 B: a headline off-centre under a tiny logo, a two-line CTA crammed against the right edge, and a bokeh dot colliding with 'Line'.

A keeps the original's centred logo, headline and CTA stack and its hierarchy, but the logo is miniscule and pressed to the top edge, the CTA nearly touches the bottom edge, and a bokeh dot clips 'Summer'. B is the same layout again: an off-axis headline and a wrapped, edge-jammed CTA with a dot on 'Line'.
